title: Using data to get other teams to follow site-impacting change guidelines
relatedProject: eBay Advertising Platform - Change Metadata & Monitoring
situation: eBay had guidelines for making site-impacting changes (announcing them, scheduling them and recording metadata), but teams outside ours followed them unevenly. As a contractor, I had no authority over those teams, and when changes went unrecorded, incidents took longer to diagnose for everyone.
task: Persuade other engineering teams to adopt the change guidelines consistently, without being able to mandate it.
action: I let the data make the case instead of arguing about process. Using the change data our pipeline collected in Elasticsearch, I measured which changes followed the guidelines and lined that up against incident and triage history, showing how much longer root-cause analysis took when a change was undocumented [confirm: the exact comparison you made]. I made the findings specific to each team, so every team could see its own numbers instead of a generic reminder. I presented them in [confirm: forums, e.g., ops reviews or team syncs] and framed compliance as something that protected their own on-call engineers, not as policy for its own sake. I also made compliance easier by having the tooling show the required metadata fields, so following the rules took less effort.
result: Several teams adopted the guidelines [confirm: number of teams or the change in compliance rate], which made the change index more complete and helped sustain the MTTI improvement. What I learned: when you can't mandate something, show each team its own data and make the right behavior the easy one.
